name: Stream

profile.campus: Stream PHXA campus, Goodyear, AZ (planned 7 buildings, 157 acres, 280 MW at full build)
profile.reading: Stream Data Centers PHX-1 sits at 2950 South Litchfield Road in Goodyear, Arizona, part of Stream large PHXA campus. Per Stream own site, the full campus is planned as seven buildings across 157 acres, targeting 280 megawatts and more than 2 million square feet at full build-out, with an on-site Arizona Public Service substation ultimately capable of 480 megawatts. As of Stream own current site content, the first two buildings on the campus were actively serving tenants while the remaining five were still in development, but Stream site does not publish a dedicated page or building-specific capacity and square footage figures for PHX-1 as distinct from the overall campus totals, so no individual capacity or square footage figure is assigned to this record, only the campus-level context. No tenant is named for PHX-1 specifically. Stream Data Centers was founded in 1999 in Dallas, Texas, originally as a technical real estate affiliate of Stream Realty Partners, a larger commercial real estate firm. Ownership has changed more recently: Apollo-managed funds announced acquisition of a majority stake in Stream in August 2025 and completed the deal in November 2025, with Principal Asset Management taking a minority stake and Stream management retaining a minority position, and Stream now describes itself as a key operating platform within the Apollo ecosystem. The company markets its wholesale, powered-shell, and build-to-suit data center model, claiming more than 90 percent of its capacity leased to Fortune 100 customers and describing a pipeline exceeding four gigawatts with more than 27 delivered developments across its US markets. Goodyear sits in the West Valley submarket of metro Phoenix, an area that has become one of the fastest-growing hyperscale data center corridors in the United States over the past several years, driven by available land, a favorable regulatory environment, and substantial Arizona Public Service grid investment, all factors consistent with Stream decision to plan a campus of this scale in that specific location.
profile.research_note: Campus-level 280 MW / 157 acre / 7-building PHXA figures sourced to Stream own Phoenix location page, explicitly not assigned to this individual PHX-1 building since no per-building figures are published. Company background from Stream own history/news pages.

profile.campus: Stream Chicago, IL submarket (Elk Grove Village, ORDA site, separate campus from Chicago II)
profile.address: 2080 Lunt Avenue, Elk Grove Village, IL 60007
profile.reading: Stream Chicago I sits at 2080 Lunt Avenue in Elk Grove Village, Illinois, internally coded ORDA by the operator. Per Stream own site, the facility was acquired in December 2017 and subsequently reconstructed, providing 31 megawatts of capacity across 155,189 square feet, with a 2024 expansion adding a further 28,500 square feet on 1.10 acres. The facility was reported fully leased by the end of 2020 to an unnamed major cloud customer. Chicago I sits in the same Elk Grove Village submarket as Stream separate Chicago II facility on Busse Road, though Stream own site treats the two as sequential, separately developed campuses rather than one shared site, distinguished by different street addresses and different commissioning timelines. A third facility, referred to as Chicago III or ORDC, broke ground in September 2025 nearby on Landmeier Road, planned as more than 1.2 million square feet across three buildings with a dedicated ComEd substation and targeted service in 2027, underscoring the submarket continued growth. Stream Data Centers was founded in 1999 in Dallas, Texas, originally as a technical real estate affiliate of Stream Realty Partners. Ownership has changed more recently: Apollo-managed funds completed acquisition of a majority stake in November 2025, with Principal Asset Management taking a minority stake and Stream management retaining a minority position, and Stream now describes itself as a key operating platform within the Apollo ecosystem. Elk Grove Village sits in the O Hare International Airport industrial corridor northwest of downtown Chicago, an area that has become one of the Midwest most significant data center clusters given its fiber connectivity, airport proximity, and interstate access, factors consistent with Stream original 2017 decision to acquire and reconstruct a building in that specific submarket rather than build new elsewhere.
profile.research_note: 31 MW / 155,189 sqft (plus a 2024 +28,500 sqft expansion), Dec 2017 acquisition, fully leased by end 2020 sourced to Stream own Chicago I page. Explicitly noted as a separate campus from Chicago II per Stream own site, and the newer Chicago III/ORDC groundbreaking noted for submarket context without conflating it with this facility.

profile.campus: Stream Minneapolis campus (Minneapolis I, sold Jan 2024, and Minneapolis II / MSPA1, still Stream-operated)
profile.address: West Creek Lane, Chaska, MN (either 1706 or 1708, exact building unconfirmed)
profile.reading: This OpenStreetMap record, tagged StreamData Center, sits on West Creek Lane in Chaska, Minnesota, part of the Minneapolis metro area. Stream own site describes two adjacent buildings on this street that could not be disambiguated from the coordinates alone this session: Minneapolis I at 1708 West Creek Lane, a 7.2 megawatt, 75,800 square foot facility opened in June 2014 that Stream own site states was sold in January 2024 to a colocation provider, and Minneapolis II, also known internally as MSPA1, at 1706 West Creek Lane, a 2.4 megawatt facility expandable by another 2.4 megawatts across 56,000 square feet split into two 10,000 square foot data halls, opened in December 2017 and, per Stream own site, fully leased to an unnamed large commercial bank and still Stream-operated. Because both buildings sit on the same short street and this record generic naming does not specify which one it represents, no single capacity or square footage figure is assigned to it individually, though both real, sourced figures are presented here for context rather than omitted or averaged into an invented composite number. Stream Data Centers was founded in 1999 in Dallas, Texas, originally as a technical real estate affiliate of Stream Realty Partners. Ownership has changed more recently: Apollo-managed funds completed acquisition of a majority stake in November 2025, with Principal Asset Management taking a minority stake and Stream management retaining a minority position, and Stream now describes itself as a key operating platform within the Apollo ecosystem, marketing a wholesale and build-to-suit model with more than 90 percent of capacity leased to Fortune 100 customers. Chaska sits within Carver County, a fast-growing exurb southwest of downtown Minneapolis, and Stream decision to develop two separate buildings on the same short street over a roughly three-year span reflects the broader Minneapolis market steady demand growth through the mid-2010s, well before the market later cooled enough for Stream to sell the earlier of the two buildings in 2024.

profile.campus: Stream Houston/The Woodlands, TX site (IAHA) - sold, no longer Stream-operated
profile.address: 4001 Technology Forest Boulevard, The Woodlands, TX 77381
profile.reading: Stream Data Centers Houston sits at 4001 Technology Forest Boulevard in The Woodlands, Texas, internally coded IAHA by the operator. Per Stream own site, the facility provided 7.8-plus megawatts of 2N critical load across a 10,000 square foot data hall within a larger building, opened in 2013 to a Tier III design standard and LEED Silver certified. Stream current locations page, however, describes this site as sold and now operating as a private data center no longer under Stream management, so this record documents the facility Stream-era history rather than its current operator or status. No tenant was named for the site during its Stream-operated years. Stream Data Centers was founded in 1999 in Dallas, Texas, originally as a technical real estate affiliate of Stream Realty Partners, a larger commercial real estate firm, confirming that lineage directly from Stream own company history page. Ownership has changed more recently: Apollo-managed funds announced acquisition of a majority stake in Stream in August 2025 and completed the deal in November 2025, with Principal Asset Management taking a minority stake and Stream management retaining a minority position, and Stream now describes itself as a key operating platform within the Apollo ecosystem. The company markets its wholesale, powered-shell, and build-to-suit data center model, claiming more than 90 percent of its capacity leased to Fortune 100 customers and describing a pipeline exceeding four gigawatts with more than 27 delivered developments across markets including Dallas-Fort Worth, Phoenix, Chicago, San Antonio, Atlanta, and historically Austin, Santa Clara, Denver, Minneapolis, and the Washington DC area. The Woodlands, a large master-planned community north of Houston, has grown into a significant secondary data center and corporate back-office market over the past two decades, driven partly by major energy-sector employers headquartered there, a pattern consistent with Stream original 2013-era decision to build in that submarket rather than closer to downtown Houston.

profile.campus: Legacy Stream asset (Richardson, TX, DFW IV) - sold 2011, no longer Stream-operated, unrelated to the later DFWA site in Garland
profile.reading: Stream DFW IV sits at 3300 Essex Drive in Richardson, Texas, a legacy Stream asset rather than a currently Stream-operated facility. Per Stream own site, the building provided 1.68 megawatts of capacity, expandable to 2.3 megawatts, across 20,000 square feet including a 10,000 square foot data hall. Stream leased the facility to an unnamed major healthcare provider in early 2011 and sold it later that same year to a real estate investment trust, whose identity could not be independently confirmed this session, though a 2011 SEC filing from Carter Validus Mission Critical REIT surfaced as a plausible but unverified match during this research and is not asserted here as confirmed. Because Stream sold the property in 2011, roughly nine years before its DFWA facility in nearby Garland was commissioned, DFW IV and DFWA should be understood as unrelated Stream projects in the same broad Dallas-Fort Worth market rather than phases of one campus, and this record should be read as documenting the facility Stream-era history rather than its current ownership or operator, which is unconfirmed. Stream Data Centers was founded in 1999 in Dallas, Texas, originally as a technical real estate affiliate of Stream Realty Partners. Ownership of Stream itself has changed more recently: Apollo-managed funds completed acquisition of a majority stake in November 2025, with Principal Asset Management taking a minority stake and Stream management retaining a minority position, and Stream now describes itself as a key operating platform within the Apollo ecosystem. Richardson sits in the northern Dallas-Fort Worth metroplex, an established telecom and technology corridor sometimes referred to locally as the Telecom Corridor given its concentration of network and hardware companies dating back to the 1980s and 1990s, a heritage consistent with this building relatively small, early-2010s-era footprint compared to the much larger hyperscale-oriented facilities Stream has built more recently elsewhere in the same metro area.

reading:
Stream Data Centers was founded in 1999. Apollo, the publicly traded alternative asset manager trading as APO, completed a majority acquisition of the company, which now operates as a key platform within the Apollo ecosystem, having formerly been affiliated with Stream Realty Partners.

The company's own site describes more than 27 data center developments delivered across the US, with more than 10 new campuses in development and site selection underway in more than 20 states. Its primary named markets are Atlanta, Chicago, Dallas-Fort Worth, Phoenix, and San Antonio. Apollo's acquisition announcement cites more than 4 gigawatts in active development, with permanent financing backing each project, and Stream states that more than 90 percent of its data center capacity is leased to Fortune 100 customers, with zero early customer terminations across its fully joint-venture project delivery model.

The registry here tracks 3 Stream facilities across two states, Illinois and Texas, a subset of the company's five named primary markets, which also include Atlanta, Phoenix, and San Antonio. Stream's Apollo-backed 4-plus gigawatt active development pipeline is among the larger forward-looking capacity figures recorded in this registry, alongside Aligned's 6.4 gigawatt current-plus-planned total and Vantage's 1.4 gigawatt Texas mega-campus.
